You'll need to create an account before you plug in and start charging. The app shows how your charge is going in real time, so you don't need to keep checking back.\n- A Chargefox RFID card also works. An EV directory lists activation by the Chargefox app or RFID, with no Autocharge.\n- Connectors: DC charging uses CHAdeMO and CCS Combo Type 2 cables. AC charging uses a Type 2 Mennekes socket, and you bring your own cable. RAA Daily\",\"url\":\"https://daily.raa.com.au/media-resources/raa-expands-ev-charging-network-at-four-city-upark-locations/\"}]\n\nRAA's charging network in South Australia is called RAA Charge. It runs entirely on the Chargefox app, which you use to find a charger, start it and pay.\n\n**How the app fits in**\n- You find a site, charge and pay in the Chargefox app, or with an RFID card. Step 1: download Chargefox for iOS or Android. Step 2: find your nearest RAA Charge site in the app or on RAA's interactive map. Step 3: charge your EV and pay through the app or with your RFID card.\n- RAA's own member app shows charger locations, details and prices on a map, but you can't use it to start a charge. Any RFID card added to your Chargefox app will work.\n- Chargefox belongs to Australian Motoring Services (AMS) and provides the software, driver support and management services for the network.\n\n**Network size and history**\n- The first 12 sites opened in early 2023, built by Chargefox in partnership with the South Australian Government.\n- RAA says it has completed the network: more than 550 plugs at 144 charging sites, from Yalata to Mount Gambier. The State Government gave RAA a $12.35 million grant to build and run it.\n- RAA calls it SA's largest electric vehicle charging network. A third-party site counted 59 DC charging locations and 142 sites with AC charging (from RAA's charger locator, 1-8-2026).\n\n**Pricing and fees**\n- RAA members get 10% off, but only if a valid membership number is added to their Chargefox profile before the charging session starts.\n- Member prices are Metro AC 40c/kWh at peak (5pm–10pm) and 33c/kWh off-peak; Metro DC 75c/66c; Country AC 42c/35c; Country DC 76c/68c.\n- Idle fees apply at all DC rapid sites in SA. After a 10-minute grace period once charging finishes, it's $1 per minute if you stay plugged in.\n\n**Hardware**\n- AC sites (7kW–22kW) have Type 2 sockets, so you need your own cable. DC sites (60–200kW) have cables attached.\n- Rapid and ultra-rapid chargers use CCS 2 plugs, and some sites also have CHAdeMO.\n\n\nREMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"b400f4c1-5085-47c3-af7a-8e6a57ec0ba2","uuid":"e484b31a-fcf9-4273-a998-9f3a67bae176","timestamp":"2026-11-19T11:45:10.245Z","tool_use_result":{"query":"RAA electric vehicle charging network app Chargefox South Australia","results":[{"tool_use_id":"srvtoolu_01Ct4WQ25WDqJYAnuyXWTGsz","content":[{"title":"EV charging stations","url":"https://www.raa.com.au/motor/motoring-services/ev-charging-stations"},{"title":"Electric vehicles","url":"https://www.raa.com.au/motor/ev-hub"},{"title":"RAA completes South Australia’s first statewide EV charging network - Each charger's owner sets the rate, and sources from 2025–26 put most DC fast charging at about 35–75c/kWh. Some AC chargers are free.\n\n**How pricing works:** Exploren is both a charging network and the software platform behind chargers owned by businesses, councils and property owners, so prices are set by each site's owner and vary widely.
